govdocs-archive_org-TheEinsteinHoaxTheDi: H. E. Retic’s The Einstein Hoax: The Disastrous Intellectual War on Common Sense attacks Einstein’s theory of relativity. The fringe work belongs to alternative science literature. Physicists dismiss its claims. The evidence for relativity is vast. The book should be read critically.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAAgentsGenera: Jeff Gerth’s piece — European Linked to Illegal Acts Shielded by C.I.A. — reports CIA protection of a criminal. The journalist’s story belongs to the intelligence archive. The agency’s secrets often leaked. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CanadaROAdmiral: Drew Pearson’s column — ‘The Day JFK Was Shot,’ on Jim Bishop’s book — is a press piece. Pearson was the era’s top muckraker. His column reached millions. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Canale-TNBarAss: This transcript — Canale’s speech before the Tennessee Bar Association, creator unknown — is a legal address. Bar speeches captured the profession’s mood. Lawyers still study such talks. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of the legal record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ClementsManning: This FBI file — Interrogations of Oswald: Statement of Manning C. Clements — is a Bureau record of Oswald’s questioning. The declassified statement is a primary source. Clements was the agent on the scene. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PresidentialPro: This item — Presidential Protection — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PublicityOswald: This FBI memorandum — Jack Leon Ruby / Lee Harvey Oswald, Victim — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. Ruby shot Oswald on live TV. The memo may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-RaidsOfficial_R: Andrew H. Malcolm’s Violent Drug Raids Against the Innocent Found Widespread is a press piece. The raids terrorized innocent families. The exposé was brave. The findings shocked readers. The file belongs to the crime archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
more-pages-from-a-journal: William Hale White, who wrote as Mark Rutherford, continues the spiritual diary begun in his earlier Pages from a Journal. These quiet reflections trace a thoughtful man's wrestling with faith, doubt, and the meaning of an ordinary life. Unadorned and deeply sincere, the entries speak to anyone who has questioned what they were taught to believe.
right-royal: Poet Laureate John Masefield brings his love of the English countryside to this novel of horse racing. At its heart is a great steeplechaser and the people whose hopes ride with him — trainers, owners, and stable lads. Masefield writes of horses with rare understanding, making the racing world vivid even for readers who have never seen a track.
perpetual-light-a-memorial: Poet William Rose Benét — brother of Stephen Vincent Benét — wrote these verses as a memorial to his first wife, who died young. The poems move through grief, remembrance, and quiet faith with tenderness and craft. More than a private elegy, the collection speaks to anyone who has loved and lost.
chaitanya-and-the-vaishnava-poets-of-ben: John Beames brings to English ears Chaitanya, the rapt sixteenth-century holy man of Bengal, and the singers who hymned Krishna in his line. Their songs of godly love stand with India's finest sacred verse. A first-rate scholar's door into Bengal's life of the spirit.
under-the-prophet-in-utah-the-national-m: Frank Cannon, once a Mormon insider and senator, exposes what he calls the political priestcraft of Utah — the church's grip on the state and its citizens. His fierce exposé made him powerful enemies and national headlines. A controversial, revealing blast from the Progressive Era.
john-m-synge-a-few-personal-recollection: John Masefield recalls John Millington Synge — the Playboy of the Western World — with personal warmth. His recollections and notes paint the Irish dramatist vividly. A poet's tribute to a fellow poet. Aran Islands summers and Abbey Theatre nights live in his memoir.
king-coal: Upton Sinclair's King Coal is his blazing novel of Colorado coal miners — their strikes, their suffering, and the tyranny of the companies. His muckraking fiction shook the nation's conscience. A powerful cry for labor justice, as fierce as The Jungle.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agostino-bern: A 1913 entry on Agostino Bernal — a name in the missionary annals. Timothy Barrett records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The missions remember their workers. A laborer in the harvest. His letters home told the mission tale.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-vandal: A 1913 entry on Albert Vandal — the French historian of Napoleon. Georges Bertrin sketches his brilliant works. His Avènement de Bonaparte won the Academy. He made the empire live again. History with a novelist's touch. His style won the French Academy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-frontal: This 1913 reference article on the altar frontal — the antependium's decorated face. Augustin Schulte praises its art. Silk and gold clothe the altar's front. Its colors follow the seasons. The altar's festive dress. Its needlework is the nuns' proud art. Its panels tell the saints' stories.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrose-marec: This 1913 reference piece on Archbishop Maréchal — the third Archbishop of Baltimore — tells his story. James McNeal wrote it up. A French Sulpician, he led the young Church. His short rule built for the future. His crowning filled the old church. Baltimore honors its French shepherd.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-belial: A 1913 entry on Belial — the worthless one of Scripture. John Francis Fenlon unfolds his dark names. The sons of Belial vexed Israel. St. Paul names the prince of darkness. The Bible's name for the devil. His children vexed the judges' age.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedictional: A 1913 entry on the benedictional — the book of the bishop's blessings. Andrew Meehan describes its solemn use. Its pontifical blessings fill the year. The old English books are famed. The bishop's book of blessings. Its miniatures delight the antiquarian.
